identity.trade: Hides and leather: Marrowick's tanneries stink for a mile, and every saddle on the outer road was cut here.

greeting: I am the headman. Nobody voted. Nobody objected.
Folk come to Marrowick for hides and tanners. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: A new face asked about the old road. I sent him the long way.
Someone paid in old coin, very old. The face on it was not a king we know.
The river runs brown below Marrowick. Fishermen go upstream.

opinions.cecily_hazelden: I would trust Cecily with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Early. Sleep is for the respectable.

dialogue.aside: Friend. Gently, now. Sit. I will make something warm.

greeting: Sit anywhere that is not wet. The wet ones are the regulars.
The Marrowick Tannery is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Nobody signs the book. I stopped asking years ago. The rooms are never empty.
The cellar is cold and the cellar is empty. I ordered more. The order came back as promises.
A pedlar lost his pack and found it two days later, repacked and slightly lighter.
Whatever you hear about Marrowick, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.zeb_kemble: Zeb has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Zeb.

time.evening: Dusk. The good hours start now.

dialogue.aside: Take something. Anything. No, a bigger something. I insist.

greeting: Quick job or good job? I charge for both.
Marrowick is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: I make locks and I make keys. I do not ask who the keys are for.
Hinges, hooks, wolf-bells. That is what sells now.
Whoever sells the best pelts in the pass has never been seen to hunt.

opinions.hanne_calloway: Hanne undercuts me. I forgive Hanne. Mostly.
opinions.kendra_elder: Kendra has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Kendra.

time.night: Night. Business is brisk. Mind your pockets.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
Marrowick is hides and tanners. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Locks are the one thing I do not stock. Customers find that funny.
Folk buy more than they need, then bring half back. Fear shops strangely.
A very good lock was sold here last week, and a very good lockpick the day after. Coincidence, say the sellers.
If trade slows, Marrowick feels it first. If it speeds up, Marrowick feels it last.

opinions.tegan_merrow: Tegan keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.zeb_kemble: Zeb undercuts me. I forgive Zeb. Mostly.

time.rain: Rain covers footprints. A blessing for some of us.

dialogue.aside: Mind the order of things, friend. There. Now we can talk.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
Welcome to Marrowick. Mind the Marrowick Tannery. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: I remember the Long Dark. Nobody asks. Nobody wants the answer.
A cart passed in the night with the lantern covered. Nobody asked what was in it.
A rider's saddle from Marrowick is said to hold a seat through a gallop and a storm.

opinions.hanne_calloway: Hanne lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.morning: Early. Sleep is for the respectable.

dialogue.aside: You have a new scar, and fewer coins than last time. Sit.

greeting: Good leather needs oak bark, time and a strong stomach.
First time in Marrowick? The Marrowick Tannery is the place to start.
rumour: Hides come in with strange scars lately. Clean cuts, not teeth.
A man in grey asked about a debt older than he is. We sent him to the ravens.

opinions.larkin_fenwick: I would trust Larkin with a purse. A small one.
opinions.silas_pickering: Silas works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Dusk. The good hours start now.

dialogue.aside: Friend. Gently, now. Sit. I will make something warm.

greeting: You smell it before you see it. That is the trade.
You did not see me. I did not see you. Lovely.
rumour: The vats turned black overnight. Not rot. Something in the bark.
The ravens have learned some people's faces. They avoid the same ones.
The tannery cat has been there longer than the tannery.

opinions.cecily_hazelden: Cecily knows the trade. I will say that for Cecily.
opinions.clem_pickering: Clem is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

time.night: Night. Business is brisk. Mind your pockets.

dialogue.aside: My friend. Come, I kept something for you. A small thing. It means a lot to me.

greeting: Everything is for sale. Even this sentence.
You will hear Marrowick before you see it. Ask at the Marrowick Tannery.
rumour: A buyer offered gold for road maps. I said they were free. He did not believe me.
The watch does not come past the third post after dark. That is the arrangement.
The Marrowick Tannery was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.hamo_rudge: Hamo knows the trade. I will say that for Hamo.
opinions.letty_stannard: Letty works hard and talks harder.

time.rain: Rain covers footprints. A blessing for some of us.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. I would say nice day, but it is not, and you would know.

greeting: Road is mud, axle is mud, I am mud. Hello.
Looking for something? I know a man who knows where it is.
rumour: Toll keepers keep changing. Their prices are the only thing that stays the same.
A debt was forgiven last week. That is how we know someone is dead.

opinions.hamo_rudge: Hamo works hard and talks harder.
opinions.letty_stannard: Letty knows the trade. I will say that for Letty.

time.morning: Early. Sleep is for the respectable.

dialogue.aside: I do not say this often. It is good to see a face I do not need to avoid.

greeting: Need a strong back? I have one, a bit used.
Quiet streets are a gift. Do not spoil them.
rumour: Someone is hiring after dark. I did not ask for whom.
Fewer guards on the pass this month. More folk who do not want to be seen.
Ask anyone in Marrowick about the Marrowick Tannery. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.hartley_underhill: Hartley works hard and talks harder.
opinions.vance_thackeray: Vance knows the trade. I will say that for Vance.

time.evening: Dusk. The good hours start now.

dialogue.aside: You came. I am delighted. I have rehearsed this expression.

greeting: Furs by the dozen, questions by none.
Strangers in Marrowick get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Found traps sprung, empty, and tracks too big to be a bear.
Folk say Marrowick was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.hamo_rudge: Hamo works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Night. Business is brisk. Mind your pockets.

dialogue.aside: Up before dawn, friend? Then you saw the best of the day. I saw it first.

greeting: Mind the snare by the gate. It is not for you.
rumour: A snare was sprung and empty, the wire bent, not broken. Not an animal's work.
When Marrowick is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

opinions.dena_rudge: Dena and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.
opinions.hartley_underhill: Hartley works hard and talks harder.

time.rain: Rain covers footprints. A blessing for some of us.

dialogue.aside: Friend, you know I will not change my mind. Ask anyway. I enjoy refusing you.

greeting: Hold your breath or hold your coin. Either way, welcome.
rumour: Wolf pelts sell high this season. So do the people who bring them.
A stranger asked at the Marrowick Tannery for the oldest person in Marrowick. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.silas_pickering: Silas knows the trade. I will say that for Silas.

greeting: Do you have a dog? I do not have a dog. Yet.
rumour: The big kids say there is a ghost in the barn. I have not checked. Yet.
A very good lock was sold here last week, and a very good lockpick the day after. Coincidence, say the sellers.

opinions.hamo_rudge: Hamo and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

greeting: I am not lost. I am exploring.
rumour: Mum says do not go past the last post. I am only going to the one before it.
Fewer guards on the pass this month. More folk who do not want to be seen.

clues.note: The lock is clean and oiled. A lock picked well looks better than one that is not.
Prints in soft mud, shoes with the heels cut down. Someone who does not want to be followed.
A good glove, left where nobody who owned it would drop it.
Prints too big for a dog, heading for the tree line.
A dragged carcass. Teeth marks, not knife marks.
A rail splintered outward, wool snagged on the edge.

stashes.say: You take three rolls of cured leather.
You loop three coils over your shoulder.
